In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of AKH in the response to oxidative stress.
the role of AKH as an antioxidant and the signaling pathways that mediate its effect in D. melanagaster.
the role of AKH in response to OS and its relationship with FoxO signaling pathway in Drosophilla.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AKH is required for protection against oxidative stress, and that it does so through the dFoxO transcriptional pathway.
AKH is a major player in the response to OS and that dFoxO acts downstream of AKH to exert its effects in D. melanagoster.
AKH plays a protective role in the response to OS and that dFoxO acts as a major mediator of the protective effect of AKH.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AKH may be involved in the regulation of dFoxO, which may act downstream of it to regulate the antioxidant defense protein sestrin in response to OS.
AKH-RNai flies have significantly less sestrin and dFoxO and thus have a higher susceptibility to HP.
knockdown of AKH synthesis in flies increases susceptibility to oxidative damage by decreasing levels of dFoxO and its downstream target Sestrin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AKH may play a role in OS response through dFoxO.
AKH is an important player in response to OS and its absence or excess may lead to increased or decreased susceptibility to OS.
AKH plays a protective role in Drosophilla melanogaster in response to OS.
